This job turns a `sid-fit` dissimilarity into clusters. It runs PAM
(partitioning around medoids) on the SID distance for each K in a range, or,
by choice, cuts one complete-linkage tree of that distance at each K. It
reports what the elbow and the silhouette say about K, and gives every
solution letters that keep their identity as K grows, so cluster A at K = 4
is recognisably cluster A at K = 5. It never fits the forest: it reads
`sid.rds`, so choosing K and pinning letters cost seconds and can be
repeated freely.

The assignments are written to the study's datasets folder and registered,
so a later job reads them with `JOIN`: a `dc-tables` job to describe the
clusters, a `vp-fit` job with the cluster as its outcome to ask which
variables separate them.

This template is **in flight**: no study has yet run it end to end.

<!-- The two values below are written by add_job() from the subject/type it
     was called with, which are also the filename's first two fields. They
     name the SET this job belongs to, and every artifact path in the
     document is computed from them, so no output path below needs editing.

     Do NOT hand-edit these declarations: the render-time guard below checks
     them against this file's own name and stops if they disagree. To put
     this job in a different set, call add_job() again with the new
     subject/type rather than editing this copy in place. -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: asis
SUBJECT <- "morphology"
TYPE    <- "sid"
.in <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(cluster)
  library(hvtiPlotR)
  library(hvtiRutilities)
})
# Nothing below is random, but the threads are pinned as in every forest job,
# so a library that does reach for them behaves the same on every machine.
options(rf.cores = 1L, mc.cores = 1L)
# The oldest versions this template works with.
if (utils::packageVersion("cluster") < "2.1.8") {
  stop("This job needs cluster >= 2.1.8; ", utils::packageVersion("cluster"),
       " is installed.\nUpdate it, then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (utils::packageVersion("hvtiPlotR") < "2.8.9") {
  stop("This job needs hvtiPlotR >= 2.8.9; ", utils::packageVersion("hvtiPlotR"),
       " is installed.\nUpdate it, then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
# register_data() takes file = from 1.5.20 (built = before) and key_cols = from
# 1.5.24 (key = before). Checked here, before
# the save chunk writes sid-clusters.rds, so an older library leaves nothing behind.
if (utils::packageVersion("hvtiRutilities") < "1.5.24") {
  stop("This job needs hvtiRutilities >= 1.5.24 for register_data(file =, key_cols =); ",
       utils::packageVersion("hvtiRutilities"), " is installed.\nUpdate it, then re-render.",
       call. = FALSE)
}
# To render a job you have not finished, leave a chunk out with the chunk
# option skip, giving the reason in quotes, or call hvtiRtemplates::stop_here()
# in a chunk to leave out everything below it. A draft lists each one in a
# callout; a final render refuses them, as it refuses an unresolved marker.
# ?stop_here has more.
.job <- hvtiRtemplates:::.job_setup(SUBJECT, TYPE, envir = environment())
.root <- .job$root
set_path <- .job$set_path
.provenance_data <- list()
# Saves a figure as <name>.png, .pdf and .tiff in this set's graphs/ folder (or `kind`'s),
# under the SAVE_FIGURES and FIGURES study choices.
save_figure <- function(plot, name, width = 6, height = 4, kind = "graphs", linked = FALSE) {
  hvtiRtemplates:::.save_figure(plot, set_path(kind, paste0(name, ".png")), width, height,
                                SAVE_FIGURES, FIGURES, linked)
}
# The draft banners, if any, and the box under the title, after all the code above.
.job$notice
```

## Study choices

Edit these values for this study before rendering.

```{r}
#| label: edit-study-choices
# EDIT: the solutions to assign letters and draw in the Sankey, smallest K
# first. Letters are carried from each K to the next, so the range must be
# consecutive.
K_RANGE <- 2:9

# EDIT: the solution this study reports, one of K_RANGE. Leave NULL for the
# first render: the metrics and sizes below are how K is chosen, and every
# section that needs K is skipped, saying so. A final render needs K. A draft
# render with K = NULL saves clusters = NULL, so a job that reads this set's
# clusters (vt) stops until K is set.
K <- NULL

# EDIT: letters pinned by hand, by solution and PAM cluster number, such as
#   OVERRIDES <- list(pm4 = c("1" = "B", "2" = "D", "3" = "C", "4" = "A"))
# PAM numbers its clusters arbitrarily, so an override is a domain decision
# written down (which cluster a paper calls A), not a fix. Read the cluster
# numbers from the sizes table's pam column, or from the last render with
#   readRDS(set_path("estimates", "sid-clusters.rds"))$letters$pm4
# list() lets the lineage rule choose. Overrides are keyed on PAM numbers, which
# sid-fit's forest decides: after a refit they go stale, so read them again
# before reusing them. To match an earlier analysis, REFERENCE below does this
# for you.
OVERRIDES <- list()

# EDIT: optionally, an earlier assignment of these patients, such as a
# published one, registered as a dataset keyed by the patient ID:
#   REFERENCE <- list(dataset = "published_clusters", col = "C7")
# The clusters at K take its letters, each matched to the reference group it
# shares most patients with (best Jaccard, one to one), and a table reports
# how well each matched. A cluster left over keeps the lineage rule's letter.
# It replaces OVERRIDES at K, so set one or the other. NULL matches nothing.
REFERENCE <- NULL

# EDIT: optionally, groups made of clusters at K, such as
#   COLLAPSE <- list(Z = c("C", "D", "E"))
# written as an extra column G<K>. Letters not named keep their own letter.
# NULL writes no group column. The letters are this render's: the lineage rule
# chose them, so they need not be the clusters another analysis called C, D
# and E. A COLLAPSE copied from one needs REFERENCE (or OVERRIDES at K) to
# give the clusters that analysis's letters first; without either it warns.
# With REFERENCE it may name only letters a cluster matched, and stops otherwise.
COLLAPSE <- NULL

# EDIT: a cluster smaller than this at K is flagged. Later per-cluster tables
# and a vp-fit with the cluster as outcome need enough patients in each.
MIN_SIZE <- 20

# EDIT: how far the K metrics run. They are drawn beyond K_RANGE on purpose: an
# elbow is only visible with points on both sides of it.
K_METRICS_MAX <- 15

# EDIT: what PAM clusters on. "sid", the default, runs PAM on the SID distance
# itself, pam(as.dist(D), k). "profile" runs pam(D, k) on the matrix, which
# treats each patient's row of distances as a point and clusters on the
# Euclidean distance between rows, a different metric that gives different
# clusters. Some earlier SID analyses ran that, so "profile" is kept for
# reproducing them, not as a better choice. sid-stability reads this from the
# saved result, so its refits always use the metric used here.
PAM_ON <- "sid"

# EDIT: how the distance is cut into K clusters. "pam", the default, is PAM as
# above. "hclust" is complete-linkage hierarchical clustering of the SID
# distance, cut at each K, cutree(hclust(as.dist(D)), k): the $clustering that
# randomForestSRC's sidClustering returns when given k. It is kept for
# reproducing an analysis that reported those clusters, not as a better choice.
# "hclust" needs PAM_ON = "sid": the profile distance reproduces a PAM analysis,
# and sidClustering cuts the SID distance itself, so the pair would reproduce
# nothing and the job stops on it. sid-stability reads this from the saved
# result, so its refits always use the method used here.
CLUSTER_METHOD <- "pam"

# Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word) and a PDF (for the publisher), and as a TIFF when ragg is installed.
# SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names
# start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("sid-clusters-sankey"). The names are the
# file names, listed for each template in the templates README.
SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE
FIGURES <- NULL
```

```{r}
#| label: sid-helpers
# Letters that keep their identity across K. The first solution's clusters
# take letters largest first. At each later K, every cluster is the child of
# the previous solution's cluster that contributes most of its patients; the
# largest child of each parent inherits the parent's letter and its siblings
# take fresh ones. An override pins a letter to a PAM cluster number.
# PAM numbers its clusters arbitrarily, so nothing here may depend on those
# numbers: clusters of equal size are ordered by their first patient (row),
# and parents hand out fresh letters in the order of their own letters.
sid_align_labels <- function(mat, overrides = list(), pool = LETTERS) {
  mat <- as.matrix(mat)
  out <- matrix(NA_character_, nrow(mat), ncol(mat), dimnames = list(NULL, colnames(mat)))
  pinned <- function(col, ids) {
    res <- stats::setNames(rep(NA_character_, length(ids)), as.character(ids))
    ov <- overrides[[col]]
    if (is.null(ov)) return(res)
    bad <- setdiff(names(ov), as.character(ids))
    if (length(bad)) {
      stop("OVERRIDES$", col, " names unknown cluster id(s): ", toString(bad), call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (anyDuplicated(ov)) stop("OVERRIDES$", col, " gives one letter to two clusters.", call. = FALSE)
    res[names(ov)] <- ov
    res
  }
  fresh <- function(taken) {
    l <- setdiff(pool, taken)[1]
    if (is.na(l)) stop("Letter pool exhausted: more clusters than letters.", call. = FALSE)
    l
  }
  # Cluster ids of column `x`, largest first, equal sizes by their first row.
  by_size <- function(x, ids = unique(x)) {
    ids <- as.character(ids)
    size <- vapply(ids, function(id) sum(x == id), integer(1))
    first <- vapply(ids, function(id) match(id, x), integer(1))
    ids[order(-size, first)]
  }
  used <- character(0)
  col1 <- as.character(mat[, 1])
  ids <- by_size(col1)
  got <- pinned(colnames(mat)[1], ids)
  for (id in ids) if (is.na(got[id])) got[id] <- fresh(c(used, got))
  used <- unique(c(used, got))
  out[, 1] <- got[col1]
  for (k in seq_len(ncol(mat))[-1]) {
    colk <- as.character(mat[, k])
    tab <- table(out[, k - 1], colk)
    # rownames(tab) are the previous letters, sorted, so a tie between parents
    # goes to the earlier letter whatever PAM's numbering.
    parent <- apply(tab, 2, function(col) rownames(tab)[which.max(col)])
    got <- pinned(colnames(mat)[k], colnames(tab))
    for (p in sort(unique(parent))) {
      kids <- by_size(colk, names(parent)[parent == p])
      # Checked against the whole column: an override may already have given
      # the parent's letter to a cluster of another parent.
      if (!p %in% got) {
        free <- kids[is.na(got[kids])]
        if (length(free)) got[free[1]] <- p
      }
      for (ch in kids) if (is.na(got[ch])) got[ch] <- fresh(c(used, got))
    }
    used <- unique(c(used, got))
    out[, k] <- got[colk]
  }
  out
}

# An identifier as text, a whole number without exponent or decimals, so an
# ID stored as a number in one dataset and as text in another still matches.
sid_id_text <- function(x) {
  out <- if (is.numeric(x)) format(x, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE) else trimws(as.character(x))
  out[is.na(x)] <- NA_character_
  out
}

# Where each clustered patient sits in the reference, matched on the IDs as
# text. Two reference IDs that differ as stored, "1" and " 1" say, pass a key
# check and become one ID here; match() would then take the first silently, so
# that stops instead.
sid_reference_at <- function(ids, ref_ids) {
  ref <- sid_id_text(ref_ids)
  twice <- unique(ref[!is.na(ref) & duplicated(ref)])
  if (length(twice)) {
    stop("REFERENCE lists ID ", paste(utils::head(twice, 5L), collapse = ", "),
         " more than once when its IDs are read as text, so its reference group is ambiguous.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  match(sid_id_text(ids), ref, incomparables = NA)
}

# REFERENCE names a registered dataset and the column of its assignment.
sid_check_reference <- function(reference) {
  if (is.null(reference)) return(invisible(NULL))
  ok <- is.list(reference) && setequal(names(reference), c("dataset", "col")) && length(reference) == 2L &&
    all(vapply(reference, function(x) is.character(x) && length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x) && nzchar(x), logical(1)))
  if (!ok) {
    stop("REFERENCE must be NULL or list(dataset = \"<registered dataset>\", col = \"<its cluster column>\").",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

# The letters a reference assignment gives the PAM clusters at K. Every pair
# of a cluster and a reference group is scored by Jaccard, the patients in both
# over the patients in either, among the patients the reference assigns. Pairs
# are taken best first, each cluster and each group once, so the match is one
# to one; a cluster left over, when the reference has fewer groups, gets no
# letter here and keeps the lineage rule's. Never keyed on PAM's own numbers,
# which change with every refit, only on the patients.
sid_match_reference <- function(pam, reference) {
  pam <- as.character(pam)
  reference <- as.character(reference)
  known <- !is.na(reference)
  if (!any(known)) {
    stop("REFERENCE assigns none of the patients clustered here: check that it holds the same patient IDs, ",
         "stored the same way.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  ids <- sort(unique(pam))
  groups <- sort(unique(reference[known]))
  jaccard <- matrix(0, length(ids), length(groups), dimnames = list(ids, groups))
  for (i in ids) {
    for (g in groups) {
      a <- known & pam == i
      b <- known & reference == g
      jaccard[i, g] <- sum(a & b) / sum(a | b)
    }
  }
  letter <- stats::setNames(rep(NA_character_, length(ids)), ids)
  score <- stats::setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(ids)), ids)
  left <- jaccard
  # A tie goes to the cluster whose first patient comes first, then to the
  # earlier group, so PAM's numbering never decides it.
  first <- stats::setNames(match(ids, pam), ids)
  while (length(left) && max(left) > 0) {
    tied <- which(left == max(left), arr.ind = TRUE)
    at <- tied[order(first[rownames(left)[tied[, 1L]]], tied[, 2L])[1L], ]
    i <- rownames(left)[at[[1L]]]
    g <- colnames(left)[at[[2L]]]
    letter[[i]] <- g
    score[[i]] <- left[at[[1L]], at[[2L]]]
    left <- left[-at[[1L]], -at[[2L]], drop = FALSE]
  }
  list(overrides = letter[!is.na(letter)],
       table = data.frame(pam = ids, letter = unname(letter), patients = as.integer(table(factor(pam, ids))),
                          jaccard = unname(score)),
       unassigned = sum(!known))
}

# Groups made of clusters. A letter not in the map keeps its own letter.
sid_collapse <- function(letters, map) {
  if (!is.list(map) || is.null(names(map)) || any(is.na(names(map)) | !nzchar(names(map)))) {
    stop("COLLAPSE must name each group, such as list(Z = c(\"C\", \"D\"))", call. = FALSE)
  }
  named <- unlist(map, use.names = FALSE)
  twice <- unique(named[duplicated(named)])
  if (length(twice)) stop("COLLAPSE has a letter mapped more than once: ", toString(twice), call. = FALSE)
  absent <- setdiff(named, letters)
  if (length(absent)) stop("COLLAPSE names a letter that is not a cluster at K: ", toString(absent), call. = FALSE)
  # A group named for a letter that stays as it is would merge into that cluster.
  clash <- intersect(names(map), setdiff(unique(letters), named))
  if (length(clash)) {
    stop("COLLAPSE has a group name that is also an unmapped cluster at K: ", toString(clash),
         ". Rename the group.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  out <- letters
  for (g in names(map)) out[letters %in% map[[g]]] <- g
  out
}

# cmdscale() returns each axis with an arbitrary sign, so a map can mirror
# between renders. Each axis is turned so that the patient furthest from the
# origin along it is positive. Among patients equally far, the one whose row
# name (the ID digest) sorts first decides, so neither row order nor render
# changes the picture.
sid_mds_signs <- function(xy) {
  key <- if (is.null(rownames(xy))) seq_len(nrow(xy)) else rownames(xy)
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(xy))) {
    far <- which(abs(xy[, j]) == max(abs(xy[, j])))
    if (xy[far[order(key[far])[1]], j] < 0) xy[, j] <- -xy[, j]
  }
  xy
}

# The name a set's clusters are registered under. Dataset names allow only
# [a-z0-9_], and SUBJECT and TYPE may themselves hold "_", so the subject's
# length is written first: (a_b, c) and (a, b_c) would otherwise share one name.
# Names that differ only in case still meet, which the save chunk refuses.
sid_dataset_name <- function(subject, type) {
  paste0("clusters_", nchar(subject), "_", tolower(subject), "_", tolower(type))
}

# One K of a hierarchical tree, in the shape of the pam() fit the rest of the
# job reads: each patient's cluster, the silhouette widths named by patient,
# and as the elbow's criterion the height at which the tree has K clusters,
# which under complete linkage is the widest cluster's diameter. pam() gives no
# widths at K = 1, and neither does this.
sid_hclust_cut <- function(tree, d, k) {
  cl <- stats::cutree(tree, k = k)
  fit <- list(clustering = cl, objective = c(swap = sort(tree$height, decreasing = TRUE)[k]))
  if (k > 1L) {
    s <- cluster::silhouette(cl, d)
    w <- cbind(cluster = s[, "cluster"], neighbor = s[, "neighbor"], sil_width = s[, "sil_width"])
    rownames(w) <- attr(d, "Labels")
    fit$silinfo <- list(widths = w, avg.width = mean(w[, "sil_width"]))
  }
  fit
}
```

## The dissimilarity

```{r}
#| label: handoff
.handoff <- set_path("estimates", "sid.rds")
if (!file.exists(.handoff)) {
  stop("No SID fit at ", .handoff, ". Render the sid-fit job in this set first; ",
       "this job clusters that fit and never grows its own.", call. = FALSE)
}
.cfg <- study_config(start = .root)
.sid_read <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(.handoff, "SID fit", .cfg, "the sid-fit job")
sid <- .sid_read$value
.provenance_data <- .sid_read$lineage$data
.provenance_artifacts <- c(.sid_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.sid_read$record))
D <- stats::as.dist(sid$dist)
# sid.rds names patients by a study-keyed digest of their ID, never the ID. The
# fit's rows are rebuilt from its recorded selection, which checks the rows and
# their key hash, and each rebuilt ID is digested and matched to the distance.
# A reader never creates the key: a new one could not match the digests sid-fit saved.
.key <- tryCatch(hvtiRtemplates:::.study_id_key(.root, create = FALSE), error = function(e) {
  stop("This study's patient-ID key is missing. Restore the study's .hvti/id_key (copying a study loses hidden files); ",
       "rerunning sid-fit would make a new key that no saved result matches.", call. = FALSE)
})
if (!identical(hvtiRtemplates:::.id_key_fingerprint(.key), sid$id_key)) {
  stop("This study's ID key has changed since sid-fit ran, so its patients cannot be matched. Rerun sid-fit.",
       call. = FALSE)
}
.up <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_upstream_job_data(.cfg, .sid_read$lineage, list(), source = "sid.rds")
job_data <- .up$job_data
.id <- .up$selection$id
.rebuilt <- job_data$data[[.id]]
# The rows were re-read to name the patients, so the data they came from joins
# the record beside what sid.rds already recorded.
.provenance_data <- c(.provenance_data, list(job_data$provenance),
                      if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join))
.at_fit <- match(rownames(sid$dist), hvtiRtemplates:::.id_digest(.rebuilt, .key))
if (anyNA(.at_fit)) stop("The rebuilt cohort lacks patients the SID fit clustered; rerun sid-fit.", call. = FALSE)
sid_ids <- .rebuilt[.at_fit]
if (any(diff(K_RANGE) != 1) || min(K_RANGE) < 2L) {
  stop("K_RANGE must be consecutive and start at 2 or more, such as 2:9.", call. = FALSE)
}
# PAM needs fewer clusters than patients. K_RANGE is the author's request and
# stops; K_METRICS_MAX only draws the metrics further out, so it is capped.
if (max(K_RANGE) >= attr(D, "Size")) {
  stop("K_RANGE reaches ", max(K_RANGE), " clusters, but only ", attr(D, "Size"), " patients were clustered. ",
       "Lower K_RANGE.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (!is.null(K) && !K %in% K_RANGE) stop("K = ", K, " is not in K_RANGE (", toString(K_RANGE), ").", call. = FALSE)
# A draft may leave K unset to choose it from the metrics below; a final report
# must name the solution it reports.
if (is.null(K) && hvtiRtemplates:::.strict_render()) {
  stop("K is NULL. Choose it from the metrics in a draft render, then set K in the study choices.", call. = FALSE)
}
cat("Patients:", attr(D, "Size"), " Clustering variables:", toString(sid$vars), "\n")
```

## Clustering over K

PAM (partitioning around medoids), the default, chooses K patients as centers
and assigns everyone to the nearest one, here by the SID distance itself. With
`CLUSTER_METHOD = "hclust"` the job instead builds one complete-linkage tree of
the distance and cuts it at each K. Either is deterministic given the
distance, so this job needs no seed.

```{r}
#| label: pam
.ks <- seq_len(min(max(K_RANGE, K_METRICS_MAX), attr(D, "Size") - 1L))
sid_mds <- NULL  # set by fig-mds when K is chosen; defined here so a skipped chunk leaves it NULL
if (!identical(PAM_ON, "sid") && !identical(PAM_ON, "profile")) {
  stop("PAM_ON must be \"sid\" or \"profile\".", call. = FALSE)
}
if (!identical(CLUSTER_METHOD, "pam") && !identical(CLUSTER_METHOD, "hclust")) {
  stop("CLUSTER_METHOD must be \"pam\" or \"hclust\".", call. = FALSE)
}
if (CLUSTER_METHOD == "hclust" && PAM_ON != "sid") {
  stop("CLUSTER_METHOD = \"hclust\" cuts the SID distance itself, as sidClustering does, and PAM_ON = \"profile\" ",
       "reproduces a PAM analysis. Set PAM_ON <- \"sid\" with \"hclust\".", call. = FALSE)
}
# The elbow and the silhouette below come from these fits, so they use the same metric and method as the clusters.
# The captions below name the method's elbow and its cluster numbers.
.elbow <- if (CLUSTER_METHOD == "pam") "PAM objective" else "Tree height"
.sizes_cap <- paste("Patients per cluster at each K, by letter; pam is the", if (CLUSTER_METHOD == "pam") "PAM" else "tree",
                    "cluster number the letter was given to")
if (CLUSTER_METHOD == "pam") {
  # The profile distance is what pam(D, k) computes from the matrix, the Euclidean distance between rows,
  # computed once here: pam() on the matrix would recompute it for every K and keep a copy of the matrix in each fit.
  .pam_x <- if (PAM_ON == "profile") stats::dist(sid$dist) else D
  if (PAM_ON == "profile") {
    cat("PAM runs on the profile distance: the Euclidean distance between patients' rows of SID distances, kept",
        "for reproducing an earlier analysis that clustered this way.\n")
  }
  sid_pam <- lapply(.ks, function(k) cluster::pam(.pam_x, k))
} else {
  cat("Clusters come from one complete-linkage tree of the SID distance, cut at each K, as",
      "randomForestSRC's sidClustering gives them when given k, kept for reproducing an analysis that reported those.\n")
  # Named sid_pam still, and saved as the handoff's `pam`, so sid-stability and later jobs read either method's
  # fits the same way.
  .tree <- stats::hclust(D, method = "complete")
  sid_pam <- lapply(.ks, function(k) sid_hclust_cut(.tree, D, k))
}
names(sid_pam) <- paste0("pm", .ks)
sid_metrics <- data.frame(
  k = .ks,
  objective = vapply(sid_pam, function(p) unname(p$objective[["swap"]]), numeric(1)),
  silhouette = vapply(.ks, function(k) if (k == 1L) NA_real_ else sid_pam[[k]]$silinfo$avg.width, numeric(1))
)
sid_metrics$objective <- sid_metrics$objective / sid_metrics$objective[1]
```

## Choosing K

The elbow is the PAM objective, each patient's distance to its medoid,
relative to one cluster. With `CLUSTER_METHOD = "hclust"` it is the tree's
height at K clusters instead, the widest cluster's diameter, relative to one
cluster. It always falls as K grows; K is chosen where the
fall levels off, which is read by eye and stated as a judgment. The average
silhouette compares each patient's distance to its own cluster with its
distance to the nearest other one: near 1 is well separated, near 0 is on a
boundary. Its maximum is one suggestion, not a rule. Neither says whether
the clusters mean anything clinically.

```{r}
#| label: fig-metrics
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste(.elbow, "(normalized to K = 1) and average silhouette by K")'
.long <- rbind(data.frame(k = sid_metrics$k, value = sid_metrics$objective, metric = .elbow),
               data.frame(k = sid_metrics$k, value = sid_metrics$silhouette, metric = "Average silhouette"))
.long <- .long[!is.na(.long$value), ]
.plt_metrics <- ggplot2::ggplot(.long, ggplot2::aes(k, value)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() + ggplot2::geom_point() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous("Clusters (K)", breaks = sid_metrics$k) +
  ggplot2::labs(y = NULL) +
  hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
save_figure(.plt_metrics, "sid-clusters-metrics", height = 5)
.plt_metrics
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-metrics
#| tbl-cap: "K metrics; the silhouette maximum is marked"
.best <- sid_metrics$k[which.max(sid_metrics$silhouette)]
knitr::kable(transform(sid_metrics, objective = round(objective, 3), silhouette = round(silhouette, 3),
                       note = ifelse(k == .best, "silhouette maximum", "")))
```

## Letters across K

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sizes
#| tbl-cap: !expr .sizes_cap
.unknown <- setdiff(names(OVERRIDES), paste0("pm", K_RANGE))
if (length(.unknown)) {
  stop("OVERRIDES names solution(s) that are not in K_RANGE: ", toString(.unknown),
       ". Name them pm<K>, such as pm4, for a K in ", toString(K_RANGE), ".", call. = FALSE)
}
.pm <- as.data.frame(lapply(sid_pam[paste0("pm", K_RANGE)], function(p) p$clustering))
# A REFERENCE gives the clusters at K its letters, by the patients they share,
# so a COLLAPSE copied from that analysis merges the groups it named (#611).
sid_check_reference(REFERENCE)
.reference <- NULL
.ref_letters <- NULL
.overrides_given <- OVERRIDES
if (!is.null(REFERENCE) && !is.null(K)) {
  .pmk <- paste0("pm", K)
  if (!is.null(OVERRIDES[[.pmk]])) {
    stop("REFERENCE and OVERRIDES$", .pmk, " both set the letters at K = ", K, ". Keep one.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  .ref_read <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = REFERENCE$dataset, id_col = .id, key_cols = .id)
  # Matched ignoring case, as every column setting is.
  .ref_col <- names(.ref_read$data)[tolower(names(.ref_read$data)) == tolower(REFERENCE$col)][1L]
  if (is.na(.ref_col)) {
    stop("REFERENCE's col, ", REFERENCE$col, ", is not a column of `", REFERENCE$dataset, "`.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  .ref_at <- sid_reference_at(sid_ids, .ref_read$data[[.id]])
  # Each clustered patient's group in the reference, NA where it has none. Saved for sid-stability, which
  # measures its refits against these groups as well as against this render's.
  .ref_letters <- as.character(.ref_read$data[[.ref_col]][.ref_at])
  .reference <- sid_match_reference(.pm[[.pmk]], .ref_letters)
  .overrides_given <- OVERRIDES
  OVERRIDES[[.pmk]] <- .reference$overrides
  .provenance_data <- c(.provenance_data, list(.ref_read$provenance))
}
.letters <- sid_align_labels(.pm, OVERRIDES)
sid_letters <- data.frame(sid_ids, .letters, check.names = FALSE)
names(sid_letters) <- c(.id, paste0("C", K_RANGE))
.sizes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(K_RANGE, function(k) {
  tab <- table(.letters[, paste0("pm", k)], .pm[[paste0("pm", k)]])
  data.frame(K = k, letter = rownames(tab), pam = colnames(tab)[apply(tab, 1, which.max)],
             n = as.integer(rowSums(tab)))
}))
.shown <- .sizes
.shown$smallest <- ifelse(.sizes$n == stats::ave(.sizes$n, .sizes$K, FUN = min), "smallest at this K", "")
knitr::kable(.shown, row.names = FALSE)
.small <- if (!is.null(K)) .sizes[.sizes$K == K & .sizes$n < MIN_SIZE, ] else .sizes[0, ]
if (nrow(.small)) {
  warning("At K = ", K, ", cluster(s) ", toString(.small$letter), " hold fewer than ", MIN_SIZE, " patients.",
          call. = FALSE)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reference
#| tbl-cap: "Clusters at K matched to REFERENCE; Jaccard is patients shared with the group over patients in either"
#| include: !expr '!is.null(K) && !is.null(REFERENCE)'
if (!is.null(.reference)) {
  if (.reference$unassigned) {
    warning(.reference$unassigned, if (.reference$unassigned == 1L) " patient" else " patients",
            " clustered here", if (.reference$unassigned == 1L) " has" else " have", " no group in `",
            REFERENCE$dataset, "`, so the match is scored on the others.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  knitr::kable(transform(.reference$table, jaccard = round(jaccard, 3)), row.names = FALSE,
               col.names = c("PAM cluster", "Reference letter", "Patients", "Jaccard"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: small-clusters
#| results: asis
# In its own chunk because a callout is markdown, which only an asis chunk emits.
if (nrow(.small)) {
  cat("\n::: {.callout-warning}\nAt K = ", K, ", cluster(s) ", toString(.small$letter), " hold fewer than ",
      MIN_SIZE, " patients, too few for per-cluster tables or a vp-fit to say much.\n:::\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: identifiability
#| results: asis
# Flags what a reader could learn about one patient, by column and count. It changes no number.
# The table counts each cluster at every K, and the Sankey draws the patients who move from one K
# to the next. MIN_SIZE above asks whether a cluster can be analyzed, and this whether a count can be
# published. A silhouette or MDS point is a distance between patients, with no value of theirs in it,
# but the silhouette table's share of negative widths beside its n is a count, once K is set.
.ks_shown <- paste0("C", K_RANGE)
.moves <- if (length(.ks_shown) > 1L) Map(c, utils::head(.ks_shown, -1L), .ks_shown[-1L]) else list()
.signs <- if (!is.null(K)) {
  .widths <- sid_pam[[K]]$silinfo$widths
  .negative <- .widths[match(rownames(sid$dist), rownames(.widths)), "sil_width"] < 0
  hvtiRtemplates:::.identifiability_counts(table(sid_letters[[paste0("C", K)]], .negative), "silhouette widths by sign and cluster")
}
cat(hvtiRtemplates:::.identifiability_notice(rbind(
  hvtiRtemplates:::.identifiability_check(sid_letters, cells = .ks_shown, tables = .moves),
  .signs
)))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sankey
#| fig-cap: "How patients move between clusters as K grows"
#| include: !expr 'length(K_RANGE) > 1'
# A Sankey needs two or more K to follow patients between.
if (length(K_RANGE) > 1L) {
  .sk <- hvtiPlotR::hv_sankey(sid_letters, cluster_cols = paste0("C", K_RANGE))
  .plt_sankey <- plot(.sk) + hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
  # The page is 6.5 in wide; the Sankey's columns need its full width.
  save_figure(.plt_sankey, "sid-clusters-sankey", width = 6.5, height = 6)
  .plt_sankey
}
```

```{r}
#| label: sankey-single
#| results: asis
if (length(K_RANGE) < 2L) {
  cat("\n::: {.callout-note}\nK_RANGE holds one K, so there is no Sankey: it follows patients between solutions.",
      "Widen K_RANGE to compare clusters across K.\n:::\n")
}
```

A cluster that keeps its letter and most of its patients across several K
is stable; one that forms and dissolves between neighboring K is not.

## The solution at K

```{r}
#| label: k-unset
#| results: asis
# The chunks below are hidden while K is NULL, so this says why the section is empty.
if (is.null(K)) {
  cat("\n::: {.callout-note}\nK is not set yet, so the sections that describe one solution are left out. Choose K",
      "from the metrics and sizes above, then set it in the study choices.\n:::\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-silhouette
#| fig-cap: "Silhouette width of every patient at K, by cluster"
#| include: !expr '!is.null(K)'
if (!is.null(K)) {
  .at <- sid_letters[[paste0("C", K)]]
  # The fit already holds the widths; pam() returns them ordered by cluster, so put them in the patients' order.
  .w <- sid_pam[[K]]$silinfo$widths
  .sil_d <- data.frame(letter = .at, width = .w[match(rownames(sid$dist), rownames(.w)), "sil_width"])
  .sil_d <- .sil_d[order(.sil_d$letter, -.sil_d$width), ]
  .sil_d$rank <- seq_len(nrow(.sil_d))
  .plt_sil <- ggplot2::ggplot(.sil_d, ggplot2::aes(rank, width, fill = letter)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = 1) + ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Silhouette width", fill = "Cluster") +
    hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank())
  save_figure(.plt_sil, "sid-clusters-silhouette")
  print(.plt_sil)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-silhouette
#| tbl-cap: "Average silhouette width and share of negative widths, by cluster at K"
#| include: !expr '!is.null(K)'
if (!is.null(K)) {
  knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(split(.sil_d$width, .sil_d$letter), function(w) {
    data.frame(n = length(w), average = round(mean(w), 3), negative = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(w < 0)))
  })))
}
```

A negative width means a patient is closer to another cluster than to its
own. A cluster with many is poorly separated even when the average looks
acceptable.

```{r}
#| label: fig-mds
#| fig-cap: "Patients placed in two dimensions by classical MDS of the SID distance, colored by cluster at K"
#| include: !expr '!is.null(K)'
if (!is.null(K)) {
  sid_mds <- sid_mds_signs(stats::cmdscale(D, k = 2))
  .plt_mds <- ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(x = sid_mds[, 1], y = sid_mds[, 2], letter = .at),
                              ggplot2::aes(x, y, color = letter)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Dimension 1", y = "Dimension 2", color = "Cluster") +
    hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
  save_figure(.plt_mds, "sid-clusters-mds")
  print(.plt_mds)
}
```

Two dimensions keep only part of the distance, so clusters that overlap
here may still be separate; the silhouette above is the better guide.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-collapse
#| tbl-cap: "Clusters at K and the groups COLLAPSE makes of them"
#| include: !expr '!is.null(K) && !is.null(COLLAPSE)'
if (!is.null(K) && !is.null(COLLAPSE)) {
  # With nothing pinning the letters at K, a collapse names this render's
  # lineage letters, and one copied from another analysis can merge clusters
  # other than the ones it meant, with no other sign (#611).
  # With a REFERENCE, a collapse names the reference's groups. A group no
  # cluster matched leaves its letter free, and a cluster that matched nothing
  # can take it from the lineage rule; merging that cluster as though it were
  # the reference's group is the mistake REFERENCE exists to prevent.
  if (!is.null(.reference)) {
    .unpinned <- setdiff(unlist(COLLAPSE, use.names = FALSE), .reference$overrides)
    if (length(.unpinned)) {
      stop("COLLAPSE names ", toString(.unpinned), ", which no cluster at K took from REFERENCE: ",
           if (length(.unpinned) == 1L) "that letter is" else "those letters are", " the lineage rule's, not `",
           REFERENCE$dataset, "`'s. Check the REFERENCE table, and name only letters a cluster matched.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
  if (is.null(OVERRIDES[[paste0("pm", K)]])) {
    warning("COLLAPSE merges this render's own letters at K = ", K, ", which the lineage rule chose. A COLLAPSE ",
            "copied from another analysis names that analysis's letters, which need not be the same clusters: set ",
            "REFERENCE to take its letters, or pin them with OVERRIDES$pm", K, ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  sid_letters[[paste0("G", K)]] <- sid_collapse(.at, COLLAPSE)
  knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(cluster = .at, group = sid_letters[[paste0("G", K)]])))
}
```

## Reading the result

A SID cluster is a region of the clustering variables where patients are
alike, found without any outcome. It is a description, not a diagnosis, and
the letters carry no order. Read the Sankey for stability, the silhouette
for separation, and the sizes for whether a cluster is large enough to say
anything about. To describe the clusters, a `dc-tables` job joins the
registered dataset below; to ask which variables separate them, a `vp-fit`
job takes the cluster at K as a classification outcome.

A job that models one row per patient, such as `vp-fit`, also sets `REDUCE` to keep the first record by the
patient ID; the line to use is printed in the save section below.

## Save

```{r}
#| label: save
# The letters, for any later job to JOIN by the patient ID. Only the ID and
# letters are written: no clustering variable leaves this job.
.csv_name <- paste0(SUBJECT, "-", TYPE, "-clusters.csv")
.dataset <- sid_dataset_name(SUBJECT, TYPE)
# A name already registered to another file or key is not this set's: two sets
# whose names differ only in case meet here. update_manifest() would follow
# that other file and report success on stale letters, so stop instead.
.reg <- .cfg$additional_datasets[[.dataset]]
if (!is.null(.reg) && !identical(.reg$built, .csv_name)) {
  stop("The dataset name `", .dataset, "` is already registered to ", .reg$built, ", not this set's ", .csv_name,
       ". Give this set a subject or type that differs by more than case.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (!is.null(.reg) && !identical(.reg$key, .id)) {
  stop("The dataset `", .dataset, "` is already registered with key ", .reg$key, ", not this set's ID ", .id,
       ". Register it again under the ID, or remove the old entry.", call. = FALSE)
}
.csv_path <- file.path(hvtiRutilities::study_dir("datasets", .root), .csv_name)
# Write to a temporary file in the same folder first, so a failed check below
# never touches a CSV an earlier render already registered. Same folder, so the
# final move is a rename on one file system.
.csv_tmp <- tempfile("sid-clusters-", tmpdir = dirname(.csv_path), fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(sid_letters, .csv_tmp, row.names = FALSE)
# Later jobs read this file back from CSV without column types, so an ID such as
# "0012345" would return as 12345 and match no patient. Read the temporary file
# back as they do and stop, removing only it, if the ID changed.
.reread <- utils::read.csv(.csv_tmp)
if (!identical(as.character(.reread[[.id]]), as.character(sid_letters[[.id]]))) {
  file.remove(.csv_tmp)
  stop("The ID `", .id, "` would not survive as CSV: read back, its values differ (a leading zero or a long number ",
       "is read as a number). No new file was kept and any earlier one is unchanged. Cluster on an ID that reads back ",
       "unchanged, or ask for the ID to be stored without leading zeros.", call. = FALSE)
}
# The solution at K for jobs that read this file rather than the dataset, such
# as vt-explain's stratifier: patients by ID digest, as in sid.rds, never by ID.
sid_clusters <- if (!is.null(K)) {
  out <- data.frame(id = rownames(sid$dist), cluster = as.character(sid_letters[[paste0("C", K)]]))
  if (!is.null(COLLAPSE)) out$group <- as.character(sid_letters[[paste0("G", K)]])
  # Each patient's group in REFERENCE, and the group COLLAPSE makes of it, for sid-stability.
  if (!is.null(.ref_letters)) {
    out$reference <- .ref_letters
    if (!is.null(COLLAPSE)) out$reference_group <- sid_collapse(.ref_letters, COLLAPSE)
  }
  out
}
.cohort <- list(n = as.integer(attr(D, "Size")))
sid_clusters_handoff <- hvtiRtemplates:::.attach_handoff_lineage(
  list(clusters = sid_clusters, id_key = sid$id_key, pam = sid_pam, metrics = sid_metrics,
       letters = lapply(stats::setNames(paste0("pm", K_RANGE), paste0("pm", K_RANGE)), function(col) {
         tab <- table(.pm[[col]], .letters[, col])
         stats::setNames(colnames(tab)[apply(tab, 1, which.max)], rownames(tab))
       }),
       # The overrides as written, so they can be copied back beside REFERENCE.
       k = K, overrides = .overrides_given, reference = REFERENCE, collapse = COLLAPSE, pam_on = PAM_ON,
       cluster_method = CLUSTER_METHOD),
  data = .provenance_data,
  artifacts = .provenance_artifacts,
  cohort = .cohort
)
saveRDS(sid_clusters_handoff, set_path("estimates", "sid-clusters.rds"))
# Only now is the CSV replaced. Order: the .rds first, so a failure there leaves the
# registered CSV as it was; then the move; then the manifest, which records the
# file that is on disk.
if (!isTRUE(file.rename(.csv_tmp, .csv_path))) {
  # rename() fails across file systems or onto a locked file; copy then remove.
  if (!file.copy(.csv_tmp, .csv_path, overwrite = TRUE)) stop("Could not write ", .csv_path, call. = FALSE)
  unlink(.csv_tmp)
}
# register_data() registers a dataset once and stops on a second call. A later
# render records the rewritten file as a new dated version instead, so later
# jobs read the current letters and their manifest check passes. invisible(): the
# captured lines would otherwise print as the chunk's value, and they open with the
# study's full path, which does not belong in a report.
if (!is.null(.reg)) {
  invisible(utils::capture.output(suppressMessages(
    withr::with_dir(.root, hvtiRutilities::update_manifest(dataset = .dataset))
  )))
} else {
  invisible(utils::capture.output(suppressMessages(
    hvtiRutilities::register_data(file = .csv_name, dataset = .dataset, role = "named",
                                  population = "SID cluster assignments", kind = "ancillary", key_cols = .id,
                                  root = .root)
  )))
}
cat("Registered `", .dataset, "`: set JOIN <- \"", .dataset, "\" in a later job to use these clusters.\n",
    "A job that models one row per patient also sets REDUCE <- list(rule = \"first\", by = \"", .id, "\").\n",
    sep = "")
```

```{r}
#| label: provenance
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat(hvtiRtemplates:::.embed_provenance(
  .in,
  data = .provenance_data,
  artifacts = .provenance_artifacts,
  run = .job$run,
  extra = list(subject = SUBJECT, type = TYPE, cohort = .cohort, pam_on = PAM_ON, cluster_method = CLUSTER_METHOD)
))
```
